KT-02.question: What CGPA does a student need in order to opt for the B.Tech (Honours) programme, and when can they opt?
KT-02.reference_answer: A CGPA of 8.5 and above at the end of the third semester; the option is exercised during the fourth semester. The student must also have cleared all prescribed courses in the first attempt; students with a 'U' or 'W' grade in any course are not eligible.

evidence.quote: Students admitted to B.Tech Programme can opt for B.Tech (Honours) programme during the fourth semester.
The student should have a CGPA of 8.5 and above at the end of their third semester and should have cleared all the courses as prescribed in the curriculum in the first attempt.

KT-02.answer_1:
To be awarded the B.Tech (Honours) degree, students must maintain an average CGPA of 8.5 [Chunk 84, p. 25]. If this CGPA is not maintained, they will be awarded only the B.Tech Degree [Chunk 84, p. 25].

The provided context does not specify a CGPA required to *opt* for the B.Tech (Honours) programme, nor does it state when a student can opt for it. It only details the CGPA requirement for the *award* of the degree.
KT-02.answer_2:
To opt for the B.Tech (Honours) programme, a student needs a Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 8.5 and above at the end of their third semester [Chunk 21, p. 8].

Students can opt for the B.Tech (Honours) programme during the fourth semester [Chunk 21, p. 8]. Additionally, they must have cleared all courses as prescribed in the curriculum in the first attempt, and students who have obtained a "U" or "W" grade in any course are not eligible for the B.Tech (Honours) degree [Chunk 21, p. 8]. Another regulation states that a student can opt for B.Tech (Honours) at the end of the fourth semester, subject to conditions prescribed by the Senate [Chunk 12, p. 6].

EX-05.question: Can attendance below 85% be condoned for a student who was hospitalised?
EX-05.reference_answer: Yes, for prolonged illness and/or hospitalisation with a medical certificate: the student must have more than 40% actual attendance, and the notional attendance (classes attended x 100 / (classes held in the semester minus classes held during the prolonged illness/hospitalisation)) must be at least 85%. Casual absenteeism and minor illnesses are not condoned.

Such cases will not come under the purview of condonation of attendance.

EX-05.answer_1:
Yes, attendance below 85% can be condoned for a student who was hospitalized, provided they have a medical certificate and their attendance is more than 40% [Chunk 61, p. 19].

While condonation is not permissible for cases of casual absenteeism [Chunk 60, pp. 18-19], there is a specific provision for prolonged illness and/or hospitalization. In such cases, a student is eligible for condonation if their attendance is calculated to be more than 40% [Chunk 61, p. 19].
EX-05.answer_2:
Yes, attendance below 85% can be condoned for a student who was hospitalized, provided certain conditions are met [Chunk 61, p. 19].

For condonation in cases of prolonged illness and/or hospitalization with a medical certificate:
1.  The student must have more than 40% actual attendance, calculated as (Actual no. of classes attended x 100) / (Total no. of classes held till date of compilation of attendance) [Chunk 61, p. 19].
2.  The "Notional % of attendance" must be 85% or greater. This is calculated as (Actual no. of classes attended x 100) / ((Total no. of classes held in the semester) - (No. of classes held during the days of prolonged illness and or hospitalization)) [Chunk 62, p. 19].

Condonation is not permissible for cases of casual absenteeism or minor illnesses if attendance is less than 85% [Chunk 60, p. 18-19; Chunk 61, p. 19].
